title: Low-Concentration Sucrose Intake During Puberty Alters Cholesterol Metabolism and Testicular Steroidogenesis in Male Mice
content: Background: Excessive sucrose intake during puberty is a growing public health concern; however, its effects on cholesterol metabolism and male reproductive function during this critical developmental window remain poorly understood, particularly at concentrations within the range of habitual human consumption. Methods: Male ICR mice were given free access to a 10% (w/v) sucrose solution from 4 to 8 weeks of age. Hepatic and serum lipid profiles, testicular gene expression of cholesterol metabolism- and steroidogenesis-related genes, testicular cholesterol content, testosterone concentrations, cauda epididymal weight, and sperm count were assessed across two independent experiments. Results: Sucrose intake selectively elevated hepatic and serum cholesterol without significant changes in triglycerides. Serum HDL-cholesterol was significantly increased, and testicular Scarb1 expression was upregulated, while Ldlr and Hmgcr expression were unchanged and downregulated, respectively. The expression of multiple steroidogenic enzyme genes—Cyp11a1, Hsd3b1, Cyp17a1, and Hsd17b3—was significantly increased, whereas Star and Cyp19a1 remained unchanged. Testicular cholesterol content was significantly elevated, and intratesticular testosterone tended to increase (p = 0.14), while serum testosterone was not significantly altered. Cauda epididymal weight was significantly increased, and sperm count was significantly reduced in Experiment 1, with a decreasing trend in Experiment 2 (p = 0.136). Conclusions: Pubertal sucrose intake at a physiologically relevant concentration selectively elevated cholesterol and upregulated testicular Scarb1 and steroidogenic enzyme gene expression, suggesting that enhanced HDL-derived cholesterol supply via SR-B1 may prime testicular steroidogenesis during puberty. A concurrent reduction in sperm count raises further concern regarding reproductive consequences of habitual sucrose consumption during this critical window.
